payload.name: Identifiers Come From the Store, Never From a Clock
payload.description: An id names something that exists. It is taken only from a successful creation; a failed creation is an error that pauses and retries, never a timestamp that stands in for the id.

principles.name: An id is a promise
principles.description: A made-up id lets later steps, seeds and checkpoints point at nothing; the failure then surfaces far from its cause.

heuristics.condition: an id appears in seeds or checkpoints that nothing can load
heuristics.action: trace it to the site that minted it and replace the stand-in with the failure

heuristics.condition: a pipeline reports success after its persistence failed
heuristics.action: make it report failure and return no local id

decision_rules.name: Ids come from the store
decision_rules.condition: code needs the id of a graph or container it just created
decision_rules.outcome: take it only from the successful creation result; never generate one from the clock or a counter

decision_rules.name: A failed creation is an error
decision_rules.condition: creation fails because the store or persistence failed
decision_rules.outcome: return the failure, with no local in-memory id, so the walk pauses and its resume retries

decision_rules.name: Reuse only what still exists
decision_rules.outcome: confirm its container exists in the store first; a dangling id means the thing is rebuilt

decision_rules.name: Empty is not an id
decision_rules.condition: a creation result has no id
decision_rules.outcome: treat it as a failed call, not as an empty default
